messages:
Priya: Quick sync request 1Q2 'prefill-orbit' pilot. Product wants steady 2k rps at ~250ms p95, tolerate 5k rps bursts for ~15m. We need cross-team agreement on prefill window, reserved burst capacity, and a documented fallback model + rollback triggers. cc @Ethan @Maya @Leo @Sam @Javier
Ethan: Thanks. Two high-level choices: dedicated prefill/reserved slots (predictable latency) or rely on autoscale + aggressive prefill heuristics. For SLA stickiness, I vote reserved prefill.
Maya: Runtime perspective: reserved prefill + KV/prefix warming works best. Propose a 12-minute prefill window and a prioritized prefix list (top 80). Also want an explicit fallback identifier that the router can apply per-request.
Leo: Infra can reserve node pool for burst but scheduling requires 48h notice. If we reserve, we need exact vCPU/GPU counts and expected hours. Also KMS onboarding if customer keys are used.
Sam: Security: KMS onboarding + audit logs are fine. We'll need a short threat-model review (<1h) and an IaC PR adding least-privilege policies for any key roles. Also confirm telemetry strips PII.
Javier: PM note: customers expect graceful quality tradeoff when falling back. We need a short doc showing expected metric delta (latency vs. semantic similarity) for the fallback model. That helps set support scripts.
Ethan: For rollout, can we do tenant-scoped canaries (percent or specific tenant ids)? That would let us validate fallback in production without full traffic.
Maya: Yes, runtime can do percent canaries plus tenant pins. Example rollout config well use in the spec: ```json
{
  "canary": {"type":"percent","value":4},
  "fallback_model":"redwood-micro-q8",
  "prefix_warm_list": ["/search","/chat/top"]
}
```
Leo: I'll spin up a 2-node burst pool and set autoscale grace to 20m. Reservation request will be submitted tonight; ETA for approval is tomorrow morning.
Priya: Action list: Priya -> open KMS ticket (#TICKET-4987) and own customer comms; Ethan -> add canary routing + doc fallback behavior by Tue; Maya -> publish prefix list + attach eval prompts and quality curve; Leo -> submit reservation with node counts; Sam -> schedule threat-model within 48h; Javier -> draft customer-facing quality tradeoff doc. Any objections?
Ethan: One more ask: define clear rollback triggers (error rate, latency, semantic-drop). Suggest: error_rate >0.5% sustained 5m OR p95 >450ms OR top-k semantic match drop >6% -> automatic rollback to previous model.
Maya: Agreed. I'll codify those as observability alerts and add a synthetic prompt set for continuous checks. Track: gen p95, error rate, semantic top-5 match, token-cost delta.
deploy-bot: scheduled: canary rollout config applied to staging at 2024-06-12T07:30Z
Priya: Thanks team. If no objections by EOD, locking scope and initiating tickets.
